title: Runner compiles C for RISC-V and returns image plus line map (/explain)
description:
As the explorer, I need a server endpoint that compiles untrusted C for RV32IM bare metal and returns a program image and instruction-to-line mapping.

Feature: Explain endpoint
  Scenario: Hello world
    Given a C hello world
    When it is sent to /explain
    Then a program image and instruction list are returned with every executable line mapped
  Scenario: Hostile compile-time input
    Given source that includes an infinite file
    Then the request ends with a limit status and the runner stays healthy

comments.author: home
comments.text: Verified on real AWS: POST /explain through the deployed proxy on a Fargate task returned a program image and instruction map for a C program with scanf/printf; the image runs correctly in the browser emulator (n=10 gives sum=55, exit 0); the for line maps to non-contiguous groups with distinct columns; no token gives 401. Adversarial review fixed a line-table DoS, aliased symbols and status mapping.

right_now_summary: The deployed `/explain` endpoint compiles C safely and returns working RISC-V images with precise line maps.
